title: Trump Falsely Accuses Obama of Wiretapping Trump Tower
synopsis: Trump tweeted that President Obama had wiretapped Trump Tower without evidence, comparing it to Watergate. Obama's spokesman called the accusation 'simply false' and no proof was produced. The claim fueled conspiracy narratives and distracted from investigations into Russia contacts.

title: Paper Towels in Puerto Rico: Trump Tosses Supplies After Hurricane Maria
synopsis: During a visit to hurricane-stricken Puerto Rico, Trump tossed rolls of paper towels to residents at a relief center, treating aid like a photo op. Images of the moment went viral and were widely criticized as callous. The incident symbolized a detached response to the humanitarian crisis after Hurricane Maria.

title: Trump Downplays Khashoggi Murder and Defends Saudi Leadership
synopsis: After the murder of journalist Jamal Khashoggi, Trump issued a statement emphasizing U.S. ties with Saudi Arabia and saying the crown prince 'maybe did and maybe didn't' know about it. The stance downplayed intelligence assessments and human rights concerns. Critics argued it prioritized arms sales and geopolitics over accountability.

title: Ivanka Trump Receives China Trademarks While Serving in the White House
synopsis: Ivanka Trump's company received Chinese trademark approvals while she served as a White House adviser, including just before her father reversed policy on ZTE. Ethics watchdogs said the timing raised conflict-of-interest questions about foreign influence and family profit. The episode highlighted blurred lines between public office and private business.

title: Jury Finds Trump Liable for Sexual Abuse and Defamation of E. Jean Carroll
synopsis: A federal jury found Trump liable for sexually abusing E. Jean Carroll and defaming her, awarding millions in damages. Though the verdict was civil, it legally established liability for sexual abuse and for attacking his accuser. The case underscored longstanding allegations of misconduct and retaliation.

title: Trump Says COVID-19 Will Disappear 'Like a Miracle'
synopsis: In February 2020, Trump repeatedly said the coronavirus would 'disappear' and even vanish 'like a miracle,' downplaying the looming pandemic. The remarks conflicted with public-health warnings and were later cited as examples of early minimization of the threat. The message added to confusion during a rapidly escalating crisis.

title: USFL Antitrust Case Ends With $1 Verdict After Trump Push to Challenge NFL
synopsis: A federal jury found the NFL had monopoly power but awarded the USFL only $1 in damages, a stunning blow that effectively ended the league. Trump, owner of the New Jersey Generals, had pushed the USFL to move from spring to fall to compete directly with the NFL, a high‑risk strategy tied to the antitrust case. The verdict highlighted the collapse of a venture driven by aggressive, publicity‑first tactics and overreach.

title: Trump Taj Mahal Bankruptcy Plan — Gives Up Major Stake to Bondholders
synopsis: Trump moved to place the Taj Mahal casino into a prepackaged bankruptcy process, offering to surrender a large ownership stake to bondholders as cash shortages mounted. The deal signaled a dramatic reversal for a project marketed as a glamorous success but burdened by heavy junk‑bond debt. The episode underscored chronic over‑leverage and collapse of a marquee Atlantic City venture.

title: Trump Castle and Trump Plaza Casinos File for Chapter 11
synopsis: Two Trump casinos in Atlantic City filed prepackaged Chapter 11 plans after bondholders approved restructuring deals. The filings reflected deep cash‑flow problems and heavy debt loads that followed the opening of the Taj Mahal. The bankruptcies added to a broader pattern of leveraged growth followed by collapse.

title: Plaza Hotel Files for Bankruptcy Protection Under Trump Plan
synopsis: The Plaza Hotel entered bankruptcy protection under a restructuring plan as lenders and creditors moved to salvage the heavily leveraged property. The filing came amid a broader debt crisis across Trump’s portfolio. It underscored how high‑profile branding masked chronic financial instability.

title: USAir Takes Over Trump Shuttle Management as Creditors Step In
synopsis: USAir and Trump Shuttle creditors agreed that USAir would manage and operate the shuttle, with an option to buy it, after Trump was forced to cede control to lenders. The deal aimed to relieve massive debt tied to the airline venture. It was another high‑profile retreat from a debt‑fueled business bet.

title: Trump Airlines Collapses — Creditors Take Over and Shuttle Ceases (1992)
synopsis: Trump bought Eastern Air Shuttle in 1988 and rebranded it as Trump Airlines, pouring money into a luxury facelift. The venture never turned a profit; heavy debt forced loan defaults, creditors took control, and the company ceased to exist in 1992. The collapse highlighted the risks of debt-heavy branding plays without sustainable operations.

title: Trump Hotels & Casino Resorts Files Chapter 11 (2004)
synopsis: Trump Hotels & Casino Resorts and subsidiaries filed voluntary Chapter 11 petitions in New Jersey in late 2004 as debt pressures mounted across the casino portfolio. The filing formalized a restructuring of heavily leveraged Atlantic City operations. It was another major bankruptcy in the Trump casino empire.

title: Trump Entertainment Resorts Files Chapter 11 (2009)
synopsis: Trump Entertainment Resorts filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection in February 2009 as the casino group’s debts and missed interest payments piled up. The filing involved multiple Trump-branded casinos in Atlantic City. It marked another bankruptcy for the Trump casino brand.

title: Trump Mortgage Collapses Within 18 Months of Launch
synopsis: Trump announced a mortgage company in April 2006 with grand promises of dominating the home‑loan market. Within roughly a year and a half, Trump Mortgage shut down as the housing market cratered and leadership credentials proved overstated. The failure underscored a pattern of hype‑first, short‑lived ventures.

title: Trump: The Game Flops After Overhyped Launch
synopsis: Trump released a Monopoly‑style board game in 1989 that failed to meet sales expectations. A year later he acknowledged the game vastly undersold projections and it was discontinued. The episode became an early example of branding over substance.

title: Trump Vodka Discontinued After Poor Demand (2011)
synopsis: Trump launched a branded vodka line in 2006 with splashy marketing, but it failed to gain traction. Production stopped in 2011 amid weak demand. The short‑lived liquor brand reflected the boom‑and‑bust pattern of Trump licensing ventures.

title: Trump Steaks Discontinued After Months on the Market (2007)
synopsis: Trump Steaks debuted through The Sharper Image and QVC in 2007 but were discontinued within months. The short run became a punchline and reinforced the pattern of short‑lived Trump‑branded consumer products. The product line effectively vanished from mainstream retail shortly after launch.

title: Trump Magazine Ceases Publication After 18 Months
synopsis: Trump launched a glossy lifestyle magazine in 2007 aimed at affluent readers, but it ended about a year and a half later. The quick shutdown added to a string of short‑lived Trump‑branded media ventures. It underscored the gap between promotional hype and sustainable readership.

title: GoTrump.com Travel Site Shuts Down a Year After Launch
synopsis: Trump launched GoTrump.com in 2006 as a luxury travel search engine powered by Travelocity, but it shut down about a year later. The brief lifespan fit the pattern of Trump‑branded ventures that flared quickly and fizzled. It became another short‑term branding play without staying power.

title: Trump Entertainment Resorts Files Chapter 11 Again (2014)
synopsis: Trump Entertainment Resorts filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy in 2014 amid continued Atlantic City casino declines. The filing was another in a long series of Trump‑branded casino bankruptcies. The brand’s repeated financial distress undermined claims of business genius.

title: Trump Offers $5 Million for Obama’s College and Passport Records
synopsis: Trump posted a video offering to donate $5 million to a charity if President Obama released his college and passport records, reviving birther insinuations despite Obama’s published birth certificate. The move framed transparency demands as a “deal” while stoking conspiracy narratives. It was widely criticized as a publicity stunt and a continuation of his long-running birther campaign.

title: Trump Tweets Climate Change Was “Created by and for the Chinese”
synopsis: Trump tweeted that the concept of global warming was created by and for China to harm U.S. manufacturing, a claim without scientific basis. The statement became a defining example of his climate misinformation and was later cited repeatedly in fact checks. It helped normalize anti-science rhetoric around climate policy.

title: New York AG Sues Trump University for Persistent Fraud
synopsis: New York Attorney General Eric Schneiderman sued Trump and Trump University, accusing the program of persistent fraud, illegal and deceptive conduct, and false promises to students who paid thousands of dollars. The suit said students were steered into expensive seminars and mentorships that failed to deliver advertised value. It marked a major legal escalation against Trump’s branded education business.

title: Trump University Forced to Drop “University” Name for Lack of License
synopsis: New York State education officials told Trump that his business could not call itself a “university” because it lacked a license and did not meet legal definitions. The program was renamed the Trump Entrepreneur Institute in 2011. The episode underscored regulatory concerns about how the business was marketed to consumers.
